themes_detail.label: Outdoor Dining Complaints Surge
themes_detail.summary: Outdoor dining complaints spiked to 6 this week, up 860% from the 0.6 weekly average over the prior 8 weeks, suggesting a sudden enforcement gap or new dining venue opening in Greenpoint/Williamsburg that is generating neighborhood friction.
evidence: 6 outdoor dining complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.6 weekly baseline (860% spike, z-score: 4.84)
This is the most recent spike in the dataset, indicating emerging issue in real time
Follows post-pandemic outdoor dining expansion but suggests current concentration or enforcement lapse
reporting_angles: Which new outdoor dining venues opened recently in Greenpoint/Williamsburg, and what complaints are residents filing?
Are DOH inspections and permit enforcement keeping pace with outdoor dining proliferation?

themes_detail.label: Street Signs Disappearing
themes_detail.summary: Street sign complaints jumped to 6 this week—a 300% spike from the 1.5 weekly average over 8 weeks—indicating either systematic removal, weather damage, or theft that may affect pedestrian navigation and traffic safety.
evidence: 6 missing street sign complaints THIS WEEK vs. 1.5 weekly baseline (300% spike, z-score: 4.5)
Second most recent spike in the dataset, appearing same week as outdoor dining surge
Aligns with long-standing CB budget request to 'improve traffic and pedestrian safety'
reporting_angles: Are street signs being stolen, vandalized, or removed due to ongoing construction (200 Kent, 20 Berry, 289 Kent rezoning activity)?
Is DOT maintenance tracking this spike, and what are the safety implications?

themes_detail.label: Tree Replacement Crisis
themes_detail.summary: New tree requests and dead/dying tree complaints both spiked dramatically in the last week to 2 weeks—tree requests up 2300% (3 vs. 0.1 avg) and dead trees up 392% (8 vs. 1.6 avg)—signaling either recent tree loss event, disease outbreak, or belated community response to long-unaddressed canopy damage.
evidence: New Tree Requests: 3 complaints last week vs. 0.1 weekly baseline (2300% spike, z-score: 8.69, severity: high)
Dead/Dying Trees: 8 complaints last week vs. 1.6 weekly baseline (392% spike, z-score: 7.44, severity: high)
Two of the highest z-scores in entire dataset, indicating statistically exceptional spike
Aligns with long-standing CB budget request to 'reconstruct or upgrade a park or amenity'
reporting_angles: Did a recent storm, disease (e.g., emerald ash borer), or construction project kill trees in Greenpoint/Williamsburg?
How long is the Parks Dept waitlist for new tree plantings, and why the sudden surge in requests now?

themes_detail.label: Unsanitary Building Conditions Spike
themes_detail.summary: Outside building and unsanitary condition complaints surged 2 weeks ago: outside building up 700% (3 vs. 0.4 avg) and unsanitary conditions up 66% (48 vs. 28.9 avg), suggesting property maintenance failures or sanitation enforcement gap in the district.
evidence: Outside Building Complaints: 3 complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 0.4 weekly baseline (700% spike, z-score: 5.42)
Unsanitary Condition Complaints: 48 complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 28.9 weekly baseline (66% spike, z-score: 5.33)
Two concurrent spikes suggest systemic sanitation or property maintenance issue, not isolated incident
reporting_angles: Are construction sites (1285 DOB permits filed; 198 new buildings) generating unsanitary debris and conditions?
Which properties or blocks are attracting repeated unsanitary condition complaints, and why isn't enforcement closing the loop?

themes_detail.label: Noise at Houses of Worship
themes_detail.summary: Noise complaints from houses of worship spiked 700% three weeks ago (3 vs. 0.4 avg baseline), suggesting either a new loud venue opening or a conflict between an existing place of worship and residential neighbors.
evidence: House of Worship Noise: 3 complaints 3 weeks ago vs. 0.4 weekly baseline (700% spike, z-score: 5.42)
Spike is slightly older than others but still statistically significant
Greenpoint/Williamsburg have diverse religious institutions; this may reflect cultural tension or new venue
reporting_angles: Which house of worship or religious gathering is generating noise complaints, and what is the underlying conflict?
How does NYPD enforcement of noise violations differ for houses of worship vs. commercial venues?
